relevance_note: Case report of one adult with arterial tortuosity syndrome plus an affected father and sibling: "A 27-year-old patient with ATS was referred to the clinic 8 years ago".
method_note: Built by hand with a small Python script in the scratch directory; every span checked verbatim against the paper. Scope: the case patient (label 'patient'), the father and the sibling (arterial tortuosity on family CT angiography; 'The family’s diagnosis of ATS was later reestablished with genetic testing'), and the previously published adult ATS patient of Aliramezany et al (ref 17) because the Discussion gives individual-level facts (adult; pulmonary artery pressure 120 to 60 mm Hg after balloon angioplasty). Not included: Santoro et al (ref 18; describes a strategy, no person-level facts), refs 6 and 7 ('adult presentations have also been reported', no detail in the text; the 51-year-old woman and variant appear only in a reference-list title, not used). No variant rows: the paper says the family's diagnosis was reestablished with genetic testing but never names SLC2A10 or a variant for this family (SLC2A10 is named only in a general Discussion statement), so no variant is tied to any person. Age: '27-year-old ... referred to the clinic 8 years ago' is ambiguous between age at referral and age at report; recorded as age at last evaluation (P27Y) with that caveat. Sex male from 'he'. Father/sibling 'arterial tortuosity' gives no site, so the aorta/other-artery checklist items stay not reported for them. Contradiction: text gives May 2018 mean PAP 80 mm Hg and PVR 20.9 WU, while Table 1 (May 2018: Before First Procedure) gives mean PAP 84 mm Hg and PVR 20.39 WU; the text values are quoted in severity_or_detail. Table 1 serial haemodynamics (patients as one column set, a single patient over five time points) were not transcribed as features beyond pulmonary hypertension. Exertional dyspnea / shortness of breath was not mapped to the 'respiratory distress or insufficiency' checklist item. Vital status left not reported (alive is implied by ongoing follow-up and consent but not stated).

Dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel was established.
Patient was treated with furosemide and antibiotics.
The patient underwent percutaneous pulmonary stent implantation for right-sided lesions in January of 2019, and total revascularization was achieved with the deployment of self-expanding stents
Medical treatment was rearranged with riociguat monotherapy in addition to single antiplatelet treatment with aspirin.
